declared_purpose: Operate assigned GitLab work with owner-verified access and guarded MR delivery. Explicit duties include incident adoption, task analysis, repository changes, review, workflow tracking and activity checkpoints. Supporting source also implements configured collaborator discovery.

data_operations.operation: Read the configured owner identity locally
data_operations.data_scope: GITLAB_AGENT_OWNER; otherwise the complete workspace USER.md text, extracting GitLab Username.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local discovery process; the extracted username is used for authorization comparisons.
data_operations.condition: Every discovery run; USER.md is read only when the environment variable is unset or empty.

data_operations.operation: Read skill configuration locally
data_operations.data_scope: Complete JSON configuration from OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH or ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; extract collaborators.accept or reviewer.ignore, accepting direct and nested config spellings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Python process memory; no configuration-file upload is shown.
data_operations.condition: Discovery and reviewer selection when the file exists; reviewer exclusions are reread during --apply.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve authenticated identity and discover work
data_operations.data_scope: Current GitLab user, assigned open issues/MRs, member-project records, project eligibility metadata and unassigned incidents. Complete returned JSON records are collected before item-level owner authorization.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requests go to the GitLab host selected by glab; responses enter the local discovery process.
data_operations.condition: Discovery runs; incident enumeration skips archived, deleting and forked projects.

data_operations.operation: Resolve collaborators and infer email-domain matches
data_operations.data_scope: Configured usernames, group selectors or email domains; returned users and group memberships. Domain matching examines email, public_email and commit_email, then retrieves matching authors' open unassigned issues.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selectors and search terms go to the configured GitLab host; matched usernames and issue records remain in the discovery process.
data_operations.condition: Only for configured collaborators.accept entries; an empty list performs no collaborator searches. A domain match establishes an email-suffix match, not verified organizational affiliation.

data_operations.operation: Infer project authorization from membership provenance
data_operations.data_scope: Item URL path and IID; agent membership username, state, access level and created_by username. Authorization is cached per project during permitted_items.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Membership queries go to GitLab; authorization decisions remain local.
data_operations.condition: Before returning eligible objects; membership lookup is bypassed when the agent username equals the configured owner. Invalid identities or incomplete data fail closed.

data_operations.operation: Persist authorization labels
data_operations.data_scope: Current object labels and required workflow-label additions/removals.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The issue or MR on the configured GitLab host.
data_operations.condition: Allowed objects lose stale workflow::forbidden; denied objects receive it and lose other workflow labels. Writes occur only for actual deltas. Label removal changes classification; it does not delete the object.

data_operations.operation: Adopt incidents and infer priority from severity
data_operations.data_scope: Incident state, assignees, labels and severity; agent user ID; derived support, workflow and known-severity priority labels.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Assignment and label changes persist on the GitLab incident; the returned incident enters local discovery.
data_operations.condition: Only after access is allowed and a fresh read confirms an open, unassigned incident. Unknown severity does not create a priority.

data_operations.operation: Read dependency links, rank work and return a reduced queue
data_operations.data_scope: Allowed issue links; inferred blocking status; kind, project ID, IID, title, URL, labels, assignee usernames and activity cursor containing updated_at and user_notes_count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Links are read from GitLab; the normalized queue is returned on stdout to the caller. The helper does not write a checkpoint.
data_operations.condition: After authorization; non-MR links influence ordering after priority.

data_operations.operation: Inspect task descriptions, notes and discussions
data_operations.source: SKILL.md workflow instructions and query examples
data_operations.data_scope: Issue descriptions, member-authored non-system notes, MR discussions, review events, author identities and project membership data. One example also requests author names and email addresses.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GitLab responses enter the agent's task context; no separate recipient is specified.
data_operations.condition: Required task analysis and activity audits; all note/discussion pages must be inspected before acknowledging cursors. The expanded GraphQL query is an example, not the discovery helper's executed query.

data_operations.operation: Persist cycle and work records
data_operations.data_scope: Acknowledged activity cursors keyed by item URL; interrupted-work checkpoints; suppressed no-op checks; retry history, pipeline IDs, commit hashes and agent bookkeeping.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Durable cycle checkpoint, local logs or memory; documentation guidance permits bookkeeping in the MR or work log.
data_operations.condition: Cursors advance only after full audits; unchanged status checks are logged locally instead of posted. Storage implementation and retention are unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Read and persist repository content
data_operations.data_scope: Repository files and history through clone/fetch, project AGENTS.md and changes needed for assigned work.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local checkout; pushed changes persist in the authorized GitLab project or agent-owned fork.
data_operations.condition: Repository work requires cloning; external upstream work requires an exact authorized URL and an agent-owned fork. Fork default branches are maintained daily. AGENTS.md is instructed to be read from main.

data_operations.operation: Publish task and workflow artifacts
data_operations.data_scope: Issues, plans, acceptance criteria, issue relations, comments, decisions, labels, assignee IDs, time tracking and commits carrying Generated-By model attribution.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Applicable GitLab issues, MRs and repositories; authorized upstream contributions use a cross-project MR.
data_operations.condition: Subject to the stated owner, assignment and comment-relevance gates. Unresolved incidents explicitly require assignment to all team members. Unassigned label hygiene is separately allowed.

data_operations.operation: Inspect MR target configuration
data_operations.data_scope: Project/default-branch metadata, protected-branch rules, target-branch records and CI YAML. CI inspection recursively follows local and named GitLab project includes, including their default-branch metadata when needed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Project, file and ref identifiers go to the configured GitLab API; returned configuration remains in helper memory.
data_operations.condition: CI inspection occurs when no explicit target is supplied and there is not exactly one protected branch. HTTP remote/template includes are rejected; inspection failures can select a validated default-branch fallback.

data_operations.operation: Create an MR and return creation evidence
data_operations.data_scope: Project, source/target branches, current-user assignment, optional title, description, related issue and draft flag. Without title/description, glab receives --fill. Output includes branch-selection evidence, merge-access rules and the MR reference.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: MR metadata persists in the specified GitLab project; structured output returns to the caller.
data_operations.condition: After target protection validation. Content generated by glab --fill is unresolved because glab source is absent.

data_operations.operation: Read reviewer candidates and infer eligibility
data_operations.data_scope: Current user, project, MR, all project memberships, closing issues and their authors, default-branch root tree/AGENTS.md, candidate user profiles, approval rules and branch protection. Human classification uses the returned bot flag.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Queries go to the configured GitLab host; identities, exclusions and eligibility decisions remain local.
data_operations.condition: Selection requires an open MR assigned to the current user. Human selection follows linked author, configured reviewer, then role/name/ID precedence. Self-review additionally requires approval, readiness and merge-access evidence.

data_operations.operation: Return reviewer-selection evidence
data_operations.data_scope: Selected reviewer ID, username and access level; project/MR identifiers, linked issue IIDs, complete ignored-reviewer list, selection rule and execution flags.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Stdout to the caller; no additional transmission or durable storage is shown.
data_operations.condition: Successful dry runs and successful --apply runs.

data_operations.operation: Persist reviewer assignment, approval and merge
data_operations.data_scope: Selected and existing reviewer IDs; MR head SHA for self-approval and merge.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The specified GitLab MR, including persistent reviewer, approval and merge state.
data_operations.condition: --apply revalidates exclusions, selected membership, identity and MR signature. Self-merge repeats approval/access/readiness checks; failed approval prevents merge.

data_operations.operation: Document optional CLI data access and publication
data_operations.data_scope: CI job logs, CI/CD variable data including MY_VAR, and release notes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI reads return to their caller; variable/release writes target the selected GitLab project.
data_operations.condition: Illustrative commands only; none is automatically invoked by the packaged Python helpers.

data_operations.operation: Create and clean up local test fixtures
data_operations.data_scope: Synthetic OpenClaw configuration files and captured test output. The owner-fallback test also invokes the real USER.md fallback when GITLAB_AGENT_OWNER is empty.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Temporary local directories and test-process memory; TemporaryDirectory contexts clean up fixture directories. API/mutation paths are mocked in the cited test helpers.
data_operations.condition: Only when tests are run; these fixtures are separate from production workflow persistence.

data_operations.operation: Require eventual forked-issue cleanup
data_operations.data_scope: A new issue in an agent-owned fork and its relation to the original issue.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The fork's GitLab issue; cleanup semantics are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: When gateway-originated work cannot be self-assigned because of missing membership; cleanup is instructed after the original issue is resolved. No supplied helper implements deletion.

potential_excess.data_scope: Issue-author name and email addresses in the expanded GraphQL example.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: GitLab response to the invoking agent/caller; no further recipient or persistence is established.
potential_excess.condition: Only if the SKILL.md example is executed; list-active-items.py does not issue this query.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Task analysis and member-note attribution require issue content and usable author identity; no supplied rule uses author email addresses or display names.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve assigned issues and relevant notes while retaining identifiers needed for authorization and attribution.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove author.name and author.emails.email from this required retrieval. This narrows data within a useful action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep author.username, issue content, activity information and complete note pagination.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unprojected work-item records, including titles and activity metadata, received before authorization and potentially belonging to later-denied objects.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local discovery-process memory, before permitted_items or adopt_incident decides access.
potential_excess.condition: Assigned issue/MR discovery, collaborator discovery and incident enumeration precede the applicable item gate.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Discovery must identify objects, enforce access and synchronize forbidden labels; denied work must not be analyzed.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Enumerate enough identity, assignment, project and label data to enforce gates and maintain denial labels.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use field-limited discovery where supported, deferring titles, activity and task content until access is allowed. This reduces data in required enumeration; denial-label synchronization remains required.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve object-URL validation, project exclusions, assignment checks and label deltas. Whether an equivalent field-limited API is available is unresolved.

potential_excess.data_scope: The entire OpenClaw JSON configuration, including unrelated settings present alongside gitlab-agent settings.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: In-memory JSON trees in the discovery and reviewer helpers; no remote disclosure is shown.
potential_excess.condition: The configured/default file exists and contains settings beyond the required collaborator or reviewer fields.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These helpers consume only collaborator acceptance selectors and reviewer exclusions.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read current acceptance/exclusion settings and detect exclusion changes before reviewer mutation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Supply synchronized skill-scoped JSON through OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, or introduce a scoped settings input, reducing the local read boundary.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain all relevant settings, direct/nested compatibility, malformed-setting failures and --apply exclusion revalidation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Individual user-profile responses for every otherwise eligible Maintainer/Owner.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local reviewer-helper memory; user-ID lookup requests go to the same configured GitLab host.
potential_excess.condition: All eligible candidates are queried before precedence is resolved, including runs that ultimately select one linked author, an earlier configured reviewer or self-review.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Deterministic selection requires human-status validation for candidates that can affect the selected result.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate project memberships, exclusions, relevant linked-author ambiguity and the selected human reviewer's identity.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Resolve candidates lazily in precedence order and omit profile lookups that cannot affect selection. These are redundant requests, not merely extra fields in a necessary request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Validate every linked candidate needed to detect ambiguity, preserve candidate ordering and fail-closed checks, and retain selected-user revalidation during --apply.

potential_excess.data_scope: Default-branch root-tree records and AGENTS.md reviewer configuration.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local reviewer-helper memory; repository queries target the configured GitLab host.
potential_excess.condition: These reads occur before self_review is evaluated, including successful self-merge selections.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document places AGENTS.md-based reviewer selection on the human-review path after self-review conditions fail.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Prove self-review eligibility or select a human using the documented precedence.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Defer repository-tree and AGENTS.md reads until human selection is needed. Omit these redundant actions on a proven self-review path.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep membership and linked-author ambiguity checks, all self-review gates and --apply revalidation; retain default-branch-only AGENTS.md reads for human selection.

unknowns: The actual GitLab host, authentication sourcing and credential transport/storage are delegated to unsupplied glab behavior. GITLAB_TOKEN is declared, but helpers do not directly read it.
Exact API response fields, visibility restrictions and support for field-limited equivalent queries are not supplied. Additional profile/content fields cannot be enumerated confidently.
Object routing uses the URL path without binding its hostname to glab's configured host; deployment host alignment is unresolved.
glab --fill content generation, server-side notifications, GitLab retention and downstream CI behavior are undocumented here.
No packaged orchestrator implements durable checkpoints, local no-op logs or full note/discussion audits. Their storage locations, retention and actual execution remain unresolved.
Clone, fork, log and checkpoint retention are unspecified. Forked-issue cleanup does not specify deletion versus closure or another action.

mr-create.py relies on its caller for owner and assignment gates; select-reviewer.py checks assignment but does not implement the owner-provenance gate. End-to-end enforcement depends on the instructed caller.
Reviewer human classification depends on GitLab's bot flag; separate service-account classification is not implemented in the supplied helper.
The regression tests provide mocked-path evidence, not live execution evidence. External linked documentation and services were not retrieved.
